Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 77 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 77, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt. Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 83 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 83, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 2004 it was given the protected status of municipal monument (no. 204019). The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.

name: Hallen van Stork
en: The Hallen van Stork, Van Gendthallen or Werkspoorhallen are five interconnected halls of the former Werkspoor-Stork factory on Oostenburg in Amsterdam.

name: Halte Aalsmeerderweg
en: Halte Aalsmeerderweg (telegraphic code: amw) is a former halt on the Dutch Aalsmeer–Haarlem railway line. It was built and operated by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij (HESM) as part of the Haarlemmermeer railway lines.

name: Hamer en Bouwershofje
en: The Hamer en Bouwershofje is a building at Marnixstraat 281 in Amsterdam-Centrum. As the front and back are identical, the building can also be approached from Westerkade 21 on the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Hangbrugmaisonettes
en: The Hangbrugmaisonettes is a block of flats dating from 1970 on the Dijkgraafplein in Amsterdam Osdorp. Until the 1950s there were horticultural businesses here. Amsterdam was bursting at the seams, and in 1958 construction began on the new garden suburb of Osdorp. In 1962 tram line 17 received the Dijkgraafplein as its terminus.

name: Havengebouw (Amsterdam)
en: The Havengebouw is an office building on the De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam. It stands in a prominent position on the IJ. The head office of the Havenbedrijf Amsterdam is based here. Other businesses, institutions and dwellings are also housed in the building.

name: Heilige Nicolaaskerk (Muiden)
en: The Heilige Nicolaaskerk in Muiden is a Roman Catholic church at Herengracht 83 in the municipality of Gooise Meren and is a national monument.

name: Heilige-Familiekerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Heilige-Familiekerk is a church building in Amsterdam-Oost. It stands on the northern edge of the garden village of Betondorp in Watergraafsmeer. This Roman Catholic church rose from 22 May 1951 at the end of the Zaaiersweg, where it connects via a bend to the Rozenburglaan.

name: Heineken Hoek
en: Heineken Hoek was a hospitality establishment in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Hemkade
en: The Hemkade is a street and event venue in Zaandam. It is the northern bank of the North Sea Canal and runs from just beyond the Nieuwe Zeehaven to Zijkanaal G, where the street becomes the Havenstraat. The name derives from the address, Hemkade 48.

name: Hemonystraat 4
en: Hemonystraat 4 is a small building on the Hemonystraat in Amsterdam's De Pijp district.

name: Herberg Zeeburg
en: Herberg Zeeburg is a former inn in Amsterdam-Oost. The inn was built in 1675 on what was then still Diemen territory, near Fort Zeeburg. Ships could moor at the inn at the so-called “Mosselsteiger”. A lively trade developed in livestock, which was unloaded there and sometimes fattened, and in fish.

name: Herengracht 107
en: Herengracht 107 is a building on the Herengracht (107) and Blauwburgwal (17-19) in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Hervormd Lyceum West
en: The Hervormd Lyceum West, or HLW, is a secondary school on the Hemsterhuisstraat and the Johan Huizingalaan in the Slotervaart district of Amsterdam (Nieuw-West). The school is a lyceum with a shared bridging year and the vwo, havo and vmbo (theoretical pathway) streams. In 2015 the school had about 850 pupils.

name: Hervormd Lyceum Zuid
en: The HLZ, also known as Hervormd Lyceum Zuid, is a secondary school on the Brahmsstraat in Amsterdam. The school is a lyceum with a shared bridging year and the vwo and havo streams. In 2026 the school is undergoing a major renovation and is using the school building on the Dongestraat.

name: Het Atelier (Rozengracht)
en: Het Atelier is a building on the Rozengracht in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam. It was formerly called “De Harmonie” and later “Lückner”, and is best known as one of the flashpoints of the Jordaan riot of 1934. It takes its current name from the fact that various clothing-company studios (in the 1960s) were housed in the building.

name: Het Sieraad
en: Het Sieraad is a multifunctional school building on the Postjesweg in Amsterdam. It is owned by the housing association Ymere. It is largely surrounded by water from the Admiralengracht, the Postjeswetering and the Kostverlorenvaart, and was built on a pentagonal plot. Since 20 January 2003 the building has been a national monument.

name: Het Wapen van Riga
en: Het Wapen van Riga is a house in Amsterdam, located at Oudezijds Voorburgwal 14. The house has a stepped gable. Houses of this type were built between about 1600 and 1665. The earliest stepped gables were in a style not yet typical of Amsterdam, the Dutch Renaissance, which is also common in Haarlem, for example.

name: Het Werkteater (theater)
en: Het Werkteater was a theatre in Amsterdam. Its address was Oostenburgergracht 75. Originally Het Werkteater was the home of the theatre company of the same name. From 1997 the building was increasingly rented out for other theatre productions and for television recordings.

name: Het witte dijkhuis
en: Het witte dijkhuis is a building on the Ringdijk in Amsterdam. The street name Ringdijk refers to a street at the foot of the dyke belonging to the centuries-old Ringvaart Watergraafsmeer. The Watergraafsmeer was agricultural land for centuries, with scattered settlements and buildings made up of farmhouses and country estates.

name: Het Zandkasteel (gebouw)
en: Het Zandkasteel is a landmark building in the Amsterdamse Poort district of Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It stands on the Bijlmerplein, enclosed by the Bijlmerdreef, the Anton de Komplein, the Hoogoorddreef and the Foppingadreef. For a long time it served as the head office of ING. Since 2017 it has been a municipal monument.

name: Hillehuis
en: Het Hillehuis is a building on the Gabriël Metsustraat, Museumkwartier, in Amsterdam Oud-Zuid.

name: Hirschgebouw
en: The Hirschgebouw is a monumental building on the Leidseplein and the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the south side of the Leidseplein with house numbers 23-31, and on the west side of the small park with numbers 2-2a. It also has a side entrance on the Hirschpassage.

name: Holiday Inn Amsterdam
en: The Holiday Inn Amsterdam (formerly the Esso Motor Hotel Amsterdam, and from 1975 the Amsterdam Crest Hotel) was a hotel on the De Boelelaan in the Zuid borough of Amsterdam. The building still stands and is used as a shelter for refugees.

name: Holland Casino Amsterdam
en: The Holland Casino Amsterdam is a casino on the Max Euweplein in Amsterdam. The building came into use in 1991. The casino is operated by Holland Casino.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 12
en: Hondecoeterstraat 12 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Hondecoeterstraat and the Nicolaas Maesstraat in the Museumkwartier.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 14
en: Hondecoeterstraat 14 in Amsterdam is a building on the Hondecoeterstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has wings on the Frans van Mierisstraat 90-94 and the Nicolaas Maesstraat 111.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 4-8
en: Hondecoeterstraat 4-8 in Amsterdam is a building complex on the Hondecoeterstraat, Amsterdam-Zuid, Museumkwartier.

name: Hoofdkantoor Amsterdamsche Bank
en: The Hoofdkantoor Amsterdamsche Bank is a building on the Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam, built as the head office of the former Amsterdamsche Bank. The Amsterdamse Bank was later merged into the Amro Bank, which in turn merged into ABN Amro.

name: Hoogduitse Schouwburg
en: The Hoogduitse Schouwburg, also known as the Deutsches Theater, was a theatre building in Amsterdam. Performances in this theatre, one of the first in the city, acted as a catalyst for Dutch theatre life. The Hoogduitse Schouwburg was built on the Amstelstraat, number 21, for the Hoogduitsche Tooneelsociëteit.

name: Hotel Boat & Co
en: Hotel Boat & Co, also known as Revaleiland 500, is a hotel on the Revaleiland in the Houthaven district of Amsterdam-West.

name: Hourglass (kantoorgebouw)
en: Hourglass is an office building in the Zuidas business district of Amsterdam. It is built against the office building NoMA House and lies next to the A10 ring road (Zuidasdok project), with its main entrance on the Parnassusweg and its west side on the Clara Schumannstraat.

name: Hugo de Vries-laboratorium
en: The Hugo de Vries-laboratorium is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Plantagebuurt, designed by the architect J.M. van der Mey and built in 1910-1912. It was commissioned by the University of Amsterdam for botany, and in 1948 it was named after Hugo de Vries.

name: Huis De Vicq
en: Huis De Vicq is a mansion on the Gouden Bocht of the Herengracht in Amsterdam, at house number 476. It was built in 1670 and was the national office of the Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds until 12 December 2022.

name: Huis Fuld
en: Huis Fuld is a monumental canal house with a rich interior at Keizersgracht 452 in Amsterdam, on the corner with the Molenpad. It was given national monument status in 1970. The building is rented out as office space, and a number of businesses are housed in it.

name: Huis met de Kolommen
en: The Huis met de Kolommen, also known as the Deutzhuis, has been the official residence of the Amsterdam mayor since 1927. The building was constructed by Paulus Godin in 1672 and lies at Herengracht 502.

name: Huis van Bewaring II (Amstelveenseweg)
en: The Huis van Bewaring II by the Amstelveenseweg (Havenstraat 6) in Amsterdam-Zuid was a penitentiary built in 1890. At the time of construction the prison lay outside the city, in the then still rural municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel. Around 1910 it came to lie within the urban area.

name: Huis Van Brienen
en: Huis Van Brienen (or Huize Van Brienen) is a building at Herengracht 284 in Amsterdam, with an exceptionally rich and well-preserved 18th-century interior. It is among the top 100 most important interiors in the Netherlands. The building has been a national monument since 1970 (no. 1795).

name: Huiszittenweduwenhof
en: The Huiszittenweduwenhof, better known as the Karthuizerhofje, is a hofje (almshouse courtyard) on the Karthuizersstraat in the Amsterdam district of the Jordaan, built in 1650. The design for the hofje, with 104 small ground-floor and upper-floor dwellings, came from city architect Daniël Stalpaert, commissioned by the so-called Huiszittenmeesters.

name: IJburg College
en: The IJburg College is a secondary school in the IJburg residential district of Amsterdam. Pupils can follow vmbo, havo and vwo courses there.

name: IJpromenade 2
en: IJpromenade 2 in Amsterdam is a building on the IJpromenade in Amsterdam-Noord. Since 25 January 2022, on the initiative of the heritage association Heemschut, it has been a municipal monument (200957). It is known as the “Paviljoen Tolhuistuin”.

name: Ir. Lely Lyceum
en: The Ir. Lely Lyceum is a public lyceum for secondary education in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Pupils are evenly divided across the streams (a third mavo, a third havo and a third vwo). In the early 2020s the school was one of the fastest-growing secondary schools in Amsterdam.

name: James Wattstraat 56-58 (Amsterdam)
en: James Wattstraat 56-58 in Amsterdam is a former church building. It was built as a votive church and used by the Christus Koningparochie in Amsterdam. The original church, with an area of 47 by 27.5 metres, was built by Roman Catholics in 1957-1959.

name: Jan Maijenstraat 11-17
en: Jan Maijenstraat 11-17 is a complex on the Jan Maijenstraat in Amsterdam-West.

name: Jan Swammerdam Instituut
en: The Jan Swammerdam Instituut (JSI), named after Jan Swammerdam, was originally a medical laboratory located in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Jan van Eijckstraat 47
en: Jan van Eijckstraat 47 is a school building from 1956 in Amsterdam, designed by the architectural firm of Cees van der Bom and Commer de Geus. The building lies between the Jan van Eijckstraat (at number 47), the Rubensstraat (15), the Adama van Scheltemaplein (1) and the Memlingstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Johan Huizingalaan 803
en: Johan Huizingalaan 803 is an industrial building in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Justus (gebouw)
en: Justus is a residential tower in the Sluisbuurt on Zeeburgereiland in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Kadijksplein 4
en: Kadijksplein 4, also known as the Koffiehuis van den Volksbond, is a building on the Kadijksplein in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been designated a municipal monument.

name: Kalverstraat 1
en: Kalverstraat 1 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Kalverstraat in Amsterdam. The building extends through to the closed-off Kromelleboogsteeg.

name: Kalverstraat 3-5
en: Kalverstraat 3-5 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Kalverstraat in Amsterdam. The building extends through to the closed-off Kromelleboogsteeg 5-7.

name: Kanaalstraat 102 (Amsterdam)
en: Kanaalstraat 102 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kanaalstraat in Amsterdam-West. It has been a municipal monument since 14 April 2009.

name: Kanaalstraat 147-149 (Amsterdam)
en: Kanaalstraat 147-149 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kanaalstraat in Amsterdam-West. It has been a municipal monument since 14 April 2009.

name: Kattengat 1
en: Kattengat 1 is the only building with an odd house number on the Kattengat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Kazerne Muiden
en: The Kazerne in Muiden was built after the adoption of the Vestingwet (Fortress Act) of 1874. The whole Muiden fortification was adapted to modern military thinking on fortress construction. Part of this plan was the building of a bombproof barracks, also known as Fort D.

name: Keesmanblokken
en: The Keesmanblokken is a municipal monument in Amsterdam-West. It lies on the Kijkduinstraat (house numbers 36-64) and the Solebaystraat (numbers 1 to 19a and 21 to 47), both named after naval battles. Space was kept free for schools when the neighbourhood was built, as a district with many children was expected.

name: Keizer Karel College
en: The Keizer Karel College is a school community in Amstelveen offering gymnasium, Technasium at vwo and havo level, atheneum and havo, with a one-year bridging period. The school is generally abbreviated to KKC and is named after Charles the Great (Karel de Grote). The school was originally Catholic and still celebrates Christmas, for example.

name: Keizersgracht 316
en: Keizersgracht 316, Berenstraat 1-3 is a corner building on the south-western side of the junction of the Keizergracht and the Berenstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building bears the name Groote en Kleine Beer, but was initially called the Gebouw William Koch.

name: Keizersgracht 318
en: Keizersgracht 318 in Amsterdam is a building on the south-western side of the Keizergracht, Amsterdam-Centrum, in the section between the Berenstraat and the Runstraat. The area is known as De 9 Straatjes (the Nine Streets).

name: Keizersgracht 554
en: Keizersgracht 554 in Amsterdam is a building on the Keizersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. On 17 June 1970 it was entered in the monuments register with the description: house with a bell gable (also called an inward-curving neck gable) from the second half of the 17th century.

name: Kerk van Holysloot
en: The Kerk van Holysloot, also known as the Holyslootkerk or Het Witte Kerkje, is a Hervormde (Dutch Reformed) church at Dorpsstraat 30 in Holysloot, in the rural area of Amsterdam-Noord. Since 2006 the church has been used by the Protestantse Gemeente Ransdorp-Holysloot.

name: Kerk van Ransdorp
en: The Kerk van Ransdorp is the Dutch Reformed church of Ransdorp in Amsterdam-Noord. The original church was lost to fire in 1715 following a lightning strike.

name: Klarenbeek (Amstel)
en: Klarenbeek is a 17th-century farm in the Groot-Duivendrechtse Polder, on the Ouderkerkerdijk on the east (right) bank of the River Amstel. Up to and including 1921 the whole of the Ouderkerkerdijk and the Groot-Duivendrechtse Polder belonged to the municipality of Ouder-Amstel.

name: Kleine Kerk (Halfweg)
en: De Kleine Kerk in Halfweg is a church building at Wilhelminastraat 15 in Halfweg. Originally a Dutch Reformed church, it received its nickname to distinguish it from the Grote Kerk on the Amsterdamsestraatweg.

name: Klokkenhof
en: Klokkenhof is a block of flats in Amsterdam-Zuid. It lies on the south-east corner of the Surinameplein and the Haarlemmermeerstraat, a street that still just belongs to Amsterdam-Zuid; the boundary lies on the Cornelis Lelylaan. Since its completion it has been an eye-catcher on the square.

name: Kloveniersburgwal 22-24
en: Kloveniersburgwal 22-24 is a national monument on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam, opposite the Trippenhuis. The two houses were built in the course of the 18th century and later merged. On the bel-étage, which has been altered several times, a travel agency has been based since 1986.

name: Kloveniersburgwal 26
en: Kloveniersburgwal 26 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is known as the Klein Trippenhuis, as it stands diagonally opposite the Trippenhuis at number 29. Both buildings are national monuments. Number 26 is one of the narrowest buildings in Amsterdam, only about 2.40 metres wide.

name: Koningin Máximakazerne
en: The Koningin Máximakazerne is a barracks of the Dutch armed forces on the Sloterweg in Badhoevedorp. Units of the Koninklijke Marechaussee (KMar) are based there and are responsible for security at Schiphol Airport.

name: Koninginneweg 1
en: Koninginneweg 1 is a building in the Oud-Zuid district of Amsterdam that has been extended over time. It lies on the Van Eeghenstraat and the Koninginneweg, beside the entrance to the Vondelpark on that street. The foundation stone was laid in September 1896 by a granddaughter of the chairman of the Luthersche Diaconessenvereeniging, J.G.

name: Koningsplein 10
en: Koningsplein 10 in Amsterdam is a building on the Koningsplein in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Korenmetershuisje (Amsterdam)
en: The Korenmetershuisje, or Korenmeestershuis, on the Nieuwezijds Kolk in Amsterdam is a former guild house, built in 1620 for the guild of corn measurers to replace an earlier guild house on the same spot.

name: Korte Marnixkade 4
en: Korte Marnixkade 4 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Kouwenoord
en: Kouwenoord is a residential tower and former honeycomb block, and the Kouwenoordweg is a street, in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The honeycomb block was named on 25 June 1969 after various farms in the Netherlands, including one in Kesteren. In the Rotterdam borough of IJsselmonde, in the Reyeroord district, there is also a street called Kouwenoord.

name: Kraaiennest (winkelcentrum)
en: Kraaiennest was a shopping centre in the south-eastern part of the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It lay below the Karspeldreef, east of the Kraaiennest metro station, and beneath the car park of Kleiburg.

name: Krelis Louwenstraat 4
en: De Krelis Louwenstraat 4 is a building in Amsterdam-West. In the period after the Second World War, housing construction was pursued vigorously through the implementation of Cor van Eesteren's Algemeen Uitbreidingsplan (General Extension Plan).

name: Kruiskerk (Amstelveen)
en: The Kruiskerk in Amstelveen, on the Van der Veerelaan 30a, was designed by architect Ir. Marius Duintjer. The church was built in 1949-1950 on the commission of the Hervormde Gemeente and was put into use on 11 May 1951.

name: Langestraat 61
en: Langestraat 61 is a building on the corner of the Langestraat and the Blauwburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Langestraat 78
en: Langestraat 78 in Amsterdam is a building on the Langestraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument since 1970. The history of the building and the gable stone set into it is recorded in the book Gevelstenen van Amsterdam (2007) by researchers Onno Broers (author) and Hans Brandenburg, with photographs by Pancras van de Vlist.

name: Lauriergracht 107
en: Lauriergracht 107 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 109
en: Lauriergracht 109 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 11
en: Lauriergracht 11 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 111
en: Lauriergracht 111 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 112
en: Lauriergracht 112 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 114
en: Lauriergracht 114 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 116
en: Lauriergracht 116 is a national monument on the Lauriergracht in the centre of Amsterdam.

name: Lauriergracht 118
en: Lauriergracht 118 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 12
en: Lauriergracht 12 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 123
en: Lauriergracht 123 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 130-132
en: Lauriergracht 130-132 in Amsterdam is an apartment building on the Lauriergracht in the Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a former church.

name: Lauriergracht 136
en: Lauriergracht 136 is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 138
en: Lauriergracht 138 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 148
en: Lauriergracht 148 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Armeens-Apostolische Kerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Armenian Apostolic Church in Amsterdam is located at Kromboomssloot 22 in the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood of Amsterdam-Centrum. From the beginning of the 17th century, Armenian merchants settled in Amsterdam, mainly in the then-new Lastage district east of the Nieuwmarkt.

name: ABN AMRO-hoofdkantoor
en: The ABN AMRO head office is located in Amsterdam at the Zuidas. At 105 metres and 24 storeys, it is one of the ten tallest buildings in the capital. As its name suggests, it is the head office of the Dutch bank ABN AMRO.

name: Augustanakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Augustanakerk, also called the Augustanahof (after the new functions the building now houses), is a Lutheran church building in the Amsterdam district of Bos en Lommer.

name: Brouwersgracht 51 (Amsterdam)
en: Brouwersgracht 51 in Amsterdam is a house on the Brouwersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Brouwersgracht is a centuries-old canal. Much of its original building stock has disappeared, including the building that stood at number 51, which was built at the request of J.J.F.

name: De Ark (Slotervaart)
en: De Ark is a church building in the Slotervaart district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The church was built in 1960-61 to a design by the architect Piet Zanstra. It has been on the municipal monuments list since 2008 and in the Top 100 of young monuments of Amsterdam.

name: Doelenzaal
en: The Doelenzaal was housed in a building at Kloveniersburgwal 87-89 in Amsterdam.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 271
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 271 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam Oud-West. Tendering for it, as a school, took place on 15 November 1909.

name: Koninginneweg 1
en: Koninginneweg 1 is a building in the Oud-Zuid district of Amsterdam that has been extended over time. It lies on the Van Eeghenstraat and the Koninginneweg, beside the entrance to the Vondelpark on that street.

name: Museum Het Broekerhuis
en: Museum Het Broekerhuis was a museum from 1882 to 1887 at Amstelveenseweg 122 in Amsterdam, showing the contents of the Broekerhuis in Broek in Waterland, collected by Aaltje Fregeres (1810-1900).

name: Sint-Rosaklooster
en: The Sint-Rosaklooster was a Roman Catholic sisters' house at Wingerdweg 4 in Amsterdam-Noord. It was built in 1926-27 to a design by A.J. Kropholler in a traditionalist style.

name: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46
en: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46 is a building on the southern edge of the Bijdorpplantsoen in Amsterdam-Oost. Staff housing once stood here, belonging to the Bijlmerbajes prison, which stood just to the north of the small complex.

name: Overtoom 13-17 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 13-17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. When the building was erected in 1890/1891 there was still plenty of commercial activity along the Overtoomse Vaart with its Vondelkade.

name: Reynders (café)
en: Reynders (also spelled Reijnders) is a café at Leidseplein 6 in Amsterdam. It is the oldest surviving café on this square and was particularly known in the 1950s and 1960s as an artists' café.

name: Stadhouderskade 129
en: Stadhouderskade 129 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by Nicolaas Vos, an estate agent by background but also an architect.

name: Stadhouderskade 74
en: The building Stadhouderskade 74 was a mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. The mansion originally served only as a residence and was designated Stadhouderskade 51N.

name: Station Aalsmeer
en: Station Aalsmeer is a former terminus station on the Haarlemmermeer railway lines: Aalsmeer - Amsterdam Willemspark, Aalsmeer - Haarlem and Aalsmeer - Nieuwersluis-Loenen, built by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij (HESM).

name: West-End (Amsterdam)
en: The West-End, later the Ambassade, was a cinema in the Amsterdam district of De Baarsjes. The cinema opened in 1933 on the Jan Evertsenstraat near the Krommert, at what was then the far western edge of the city. It is not known whether the name West-End refers to the London nightlife district of the same name.

name: Kantoorgebouw Van Leer
en: The former office building of Van Leer's Vatenfabrieken lies on the Amsterdamseweg in Amstelveen. It was built in 1958 to a design by Marcel Breuer as the headquarters of the company Van Leer.

name: WG-Plein
en: The WG-Plein is a square in Oud-West, Amsterdam.

name: Wielingenstraat
en: The Wielingenstraat is a street in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. The street runs from the Scheldeplein to the Boerenwetering, where it becomes the Diepenbrockstraat via the Jeroen Oerlemansbrug. Along the street are houses and the RAI Amsterdam exhibition and congress complex.

name: Wijde Heisteeg
en: The Wijde Heisteeg is a short alley in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Willem de Zwijgerlaan (Amsterdam)
en: The Willem de Zwijgerlaan is an important through street in Amsterdam-West, in the districts of the Baarsjes and Bos en Lommer. The street is named after William of Orange. It was built in the 1930s and lies on the former territory of the municipality of Sloten (annexed in 1921).

name: Willem Frederik Hermansstraat
en: The Willem Frederik Hermansstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum on the Oosterdokseiland, also known as the 'PTT-eiland'.

name: Willem Frogerstraat
en: The Willem Frogerstraat is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street is named after the engineer Willem Anthonie Froger.

name: Willem Kesstraat
en: The Willem Kesstraat is a street in the Prinses Irenebuurt in Buitenveldert, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Willem Leevendstraat
en: The Willem Leevendstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West.

name: Willem van Weldammelaan
en: The Willem van Weldammelaan is a street in the Buitenveldert district, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Willemsparkweg
en: The Willemsparkweg is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, indirectly named after King William I.

name: Wiltzanghlaan
en: The Wiltzanghlaan is a street in the Amsterdam district of Bos en Lommer. By council decisions of 20 April 1939, 6 October 1948 and 9 July 1952, the street was named after the poem Wiltzangh by Joost van den Vondel. The street has a roughly east-west orientation.

name: Windroosplein
en: The Windroosplein is a square in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Wingerdweg
en: The Wingerdweg is a street in Amsterdam-Noord. The road begins at the Hagedoornweg by the Sint-Rosaklooster. It then curves gently towards the Johan van Hasseltweg, which it crosses at a different level (under bridge 494). It ends at the Sneeuwbalweg, although on the other side it has a continuation called the Ogentrooststraat.

name: Winterdijkstraat
en: The Winterdijkstraat is a relatively short street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Witte de Withplein (Amsterdam)
en: The Witte de Withplein is a square in Amsterdam-West, in the Chassébuurt.

name: Witte de Withstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Witte de Withstraat is a street in the Admiralenbuurt of Amsterdam-West. The street runs north from the Postjesweg by the Kinkerbrug to the Jan Evertsenstraat, at the Admiraal de Ruyterweg. Its architecture is characterised by the Amsterdam School.

name: Witte Klok
en: Witte Klok is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Wittenburgergracht
en: The Wittenburgergracht is part of a through traffic road in the centre of Amsterdam, lying between the Kattenburgergracht and the Oostenburgergracht. Together with these two streets, which lie in line with one another, the Wittenburgergracht forms the so-called Eilandenboulevard.

name: Wodanstraat
en: The Wodanstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid. The barely fifty-metre-long street received its name by council decision of 19 December 1929, a naming after the chief god Wodan. In the north the street begins as a side street of the Argonautenstraat and runs south to the Stadionkade, Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Wormerveerstraat (Amsterdam)
en: Wormerveerstraat is a street in the Amsterdam Spaarndammerbuurt, named after the village of the same name in the Zaanstreek in North Holland. The street runs from the Knollendamstraat to the Adrichemstraat. The streets in the Spaarndammerbuurt are named after places north-west of Amsterdam.

name: Zaaiersweg
en: The Zaaiersweg is a street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Zaandammerplein
en: The Zaandammerplein in the Spaarndammerbuurt in Amsterdam-West was named in 1917 after the place Zaandam. The square has striking architecture from the 1920s by Karel de Bazel. Many communists lived around the square, which was known as the 'Rode Plein' (Red Square). On 1 May, red flags hung almost everywhere.

name: Zaanhof
en: The Zaanhof lies in the borough of Westerpark, in the Spaarndammerbuurt in Amsterdam-West, and was named in 1917 after the river Zaan. The 82 stacked houses in the Rationalism or Berlagianism style are all national monuments.

name: Zaanstraat
en: The Zaanstraat is a street in the Spaarndammerbuurt in Amsterdam-West. Until 1877 the area was part of the municipality of Sloten, but that year it was annexed by Amsterdam, and by council decision of 1 February 1888 it was given the name Houtrijkkade.

name: Zamenhofstraat
en: The Zamenhofstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Noord. It lies between the Meeuwenlaan and the Nieuwendammerkade. The street, which winds from corner to corner, has only even house numbers. Alongside the Vogeldorp residential neighbourhood, the Zamenhofstraat also has a section of businesses.

name: Zandhoek (Amsterdam)
en: The Zandhoek is a link between the Grote Bickersstraat and Bokkinghangen in Amsterdam. The street (in fact a quay) on the Westerdok lies on the Realeneiland and takes its name from the sand ships that once unloaded there. The Zandhoek was the home of the well-known Amsterdam city photographer Jacob Olie, who began taking photographs here.

name: Zeelandstraat
en: The Zeelandstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, Buitenveldert.

name: Zomerdijkstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Zomerdijkstraat is a relatively short street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Zonneplein
en: The Zonneplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord, in the Tuindorp Oostzaan district.

name: Zonneweg (Amsterdam)
en: The Zonneweg is a street in Amsterdam-Noord, Tuindorp Oostzaan.

name: Zoutkeetsplein
en: The Zoutkeetsplein is a square in Amsterdam-West.

name: Zuidelijke Wandelweg
en: The Zuidelijke Wandelweg is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Zuidplein (Amsterdam)
en: The Zuidplein in Amsterdam-Zuid is the forecourt of Amsterdam Zuid station. The square lies in the Zuidas area. On the other side of Station Zuid lies the Gustav Mahlerplein. The square was already planned in 1917 in the Plan Zuid by H.P. Berlage as a large forecourt for a grand Zuiderstation.

name: Zuivelplein (Amsterdam)
en: The Zuivelplein is a square and street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Zwanenplein
en: The Zwanenplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord. It lies in the Vogelbuurt-Zuid, within the larger Vogeldorp; it has been a municipal monument since 2000 and, since 2014, part of the Amsterdam-Noord national protected townscape. The former Bethlehemkerk in the middle of the square is itself a national monument (508434).

name: Akersingel
en: The Akersingel is a street in the De Aker district of the Amsterdam borough of Nieuw-West. The street runs from the Ecuplein to the Matterhorn and is named after the district it runs through. Since 2001, tram line 1 has run via the Ecuplein and on along the Akersingel to the new terminus at the Matterhorn in De Aker.

name: Albardakade
en: The Albardakade is a quay in the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. The Albardakade, which received its name in 2001, does not form one of the two quays of the Albardagracht. The short street, under 100 metres long with house numbers 3 to 9, forms the south quay of a dead-end side branch of that Albardagracht.

name: Antony Moddermanstraat
en: The Antony Moddermanstraat is an important through street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It begins after the Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan/Slotermeerlaan traffic square and runs west, after which, past bridge 627 at the Eendrachtspark, it becomes the Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat in the Geuzenveld district.

name: Belgiëplein
en: The Belgiëplein in Amsterdam-Nieuw Sloten received its name on 2 October 1991 and is named after the West European country of Belgium. The street names in Nieuw Sloten are taken from places and regions in Belgium. The Belgiëplein is the shopping centre and heart of the Nieuw Sloten district.

name: Brandslangstraat
en: The Brandslangstraat is a street in the Cruquiuswerf neighbourhood in the Eastern Harbour Area in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Brettenpad
en: The Brettenpad is a cycling and walking path in Amsterdam. It is about 7.7 km long and is included in the network of through cycle routes in the province of North Holland. The path runs from the Westerpark through Sloterdijk and past the nature reserve De Lange Bretten to the Westelijk Havengebied.

name: Burgemeester Van de Pollstraat
en: The Burgemeester Van de Pollstraat is a street in Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It runs parallel to the Burgemeester Cramergracht, from the Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht to the Jan Evertsenstraat. Its continuation is the Oostoever.

name: Burgemeester Van Leeuwenlaan
en: The Burgemeester Van Leeuwenlaan is a street in Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It begins at the Antony Moddermanstraat and continues to the Confuciusplein. The street is crossed by the Lodewijk van Deysselstraat and the Burgemeester Röellstraat.

name: Christian Neefestraat
en: The Christian Neefestraat is a dead-end street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Christoffel Plantijnpad
en: The Christoffel Plantijnpad (and the Christoffel Plantijngracht) in Amsterdam-Slotervaart have been named since 1955 after the South Netherlandish printer and lexicographer Christoffel Plantijn (1514-1589), who owned a famous printing and publishing house in Antwerp.

name: Confuciusplein
en: The Confuciusplein is a square in the Amsterdam district of Slotermeer. It is named after the Chinese philosopher Confucius. The square lies in the south-west of Slotermeer, at the point where the Savornin Lohmanstraat curves left and becomes the Burgemeester Van Leeuwenlaan. On the north side of the square runs the Socratesstraat.

name: Cornelis Vermuydenstraat
en: The Cornelis Vermuydenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum. Named after the Zeeland hydraulic engineer Cornelis Vermuyden, it was built in the 2010s. It was laid out as a continuation of the start of the Blankenstraat, which had previously dead-ended here.

name: Dapperstraat
en: The Dapperstraat is the main street of the Dapperbuurt in the borough of Amsterdam-Oost. Like the Dapperplein, the street is named after the Africa expert Olfert Dapper. The street runs from the Mauritskade to the Domselaerstraat.

name: De Savornin Lohmanstraat
en: De Savornin Lohmanstraat is the name of a large number of streets in the Netherlands. These streets are named after the statesman Alexander de Savornin Lohman. In The Hague there is the De Savornin Lohmanplein and the De Savornin Lohmanlaan, and the latter also exists in Zwolle, where it runs from the Troelstralaan to the Thorbeckelaan.

name: De Wieden (Amsterdam)
en: De Wieden is a cycle and footpath with a canal running down the middle, and since 2021 also a small park, in the De Kleine Wereld neighbourhood of the Buikslotermeer district in Amsterdam-Noord. The path has only one address, where a small house from 1967 stands. The other houses all have addresses on the surrounding streets.

name: De Grote Geusplein
en: De Grote Geusplein is a square in the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. It lies in the centre of the district, close to the Lambertus Zijlplein and the terminus of tram line 13.

name: Elpermeerpad
en: The Elpermeerpad is a footpath and cycle path in Amsterdam-Noord. It begins in the urban development of Amsterdam-Noord, at the high-rise flats on the Elpermeer. It then passes under Rijksweg 10 (better known as the Ringweg-Noord) by the Elpermeerpadbrug and continues as far as the Buikslotermeerdijk.

name: Elsrijkdreef
en: The Elsrijkdreef links the Daalwijkdreef with the Bijlmerdreef in the north-east of the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Februariplein
en: The Februariplein is a city square in Amsterdam-Centrum. The square is pedestrian-only.

name: Gare du Nord (straat)
en: Gare du Nord is the name of a Dutch street in the new 'Centrumgebied' (city centre area) of Amsterdam-Noord (CAN). The new school building Community College Noord, which since 2012 has housed the Bredero Mavo and a branch of the ROC van Amsterdam (MBO College Noord), was given this address.

name: Groesbeekdreef
en: The Groesbeekdreef is a dreef in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Originally the dreef was fully elevated, in line with the principles of the urban development plan for the Bijlmermeer, and was intended exclusively for fast traffic. It opened on 10 August 1969.

name: Gulden Kruispad
en: The Gulden Kruispad is a cycle path and street in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The cycle path begins at the Burgemeester Stramanweg, near Sportpark De Toekomst. It then follows the Hoogoorddreef, passes under the railway and, near the Amsterdamse Poort, joins the Abcouderpad. It then runs, among other places, through the Nelson Mandelapark and Ganzenhoef.

name: Hella Haasseplein
en: The Hella Haasseplein is a square in Amsterdam-Centrum. Although officially listed as a square, it is in fact the small triangular forecourt of the central building of the Openbare Bibliotheek Amsterdam, Oosterdokskade 143. Only one building stands on the square, the library mentioned, which kept its original address.

name: Hoptille (Amsterdam)
en: Hoptille is a residential neighbourhood in the H-buurt of Amsterdam Zuidoost, lying between the Amsterdamse Poort / Haardstee and Heesterveld, east of the railway line to Utrecht, within walking distance of Bijlmer ArenA station and Bullewijk metro station. The district was completed in 1981 and has 333 homes.

name: Humberto Delgadoplein
en: The Humberto Delgadoplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It was not on the original plans for the district of Bijlmermeer, which was built in the 1960s. At that time there was green space here, west of the honeycomb flat Florijn.

name: Jan Herman van Heekweg
en: The Jan Herman van Heekweg, or J.H. van Heekweg, is a through street in the Buikslotermeer district of Amsterdam-Noord, named after the textile manufacturer Jan Herman van Heek.

name: Johannes Meewisstraat
en: The Johannes Meewisstraat is a street in the Slotermeer-Noordoost district of Amsterdam. It is named after the resistance fighter Johan Meewis. The street runs from the north end of the Burgemeester Fockstraat, via a bend, to the Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan.

name: Kempering
en: Kempering is a street and residential tower in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The street received its name on 25 June 1969 and was named after a farm near Reutum, in the municipality of Tubbergen.

name: Klieverink
en: Klieverink is a residential tower and former honeycomb flat in Amsterdam-Zuidoost, and the Klieverinkweg is a street there. The honeycomb flat received its name on 25 June 1969 and was named after the farm Klievering/Klieverink in the municipality of Losser.

name: Kostverlorenstraat
en: The Kostverlorenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West and is about 200 metres long. It forms the link between the Frederik Hendrikbuurt and the Staatsliedenbuurt. The street begins at the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen and runs in a curved arm shape to the Van Hallbrug over the Kostverlorenvaart.

name: Kwakersplein
en: The Kwakersplein is a square in Amsterdam-West. It lies in the Da Costabuurt, along the Bilderdijkstraat in line with the Potgieterstraat. After the bridge over the Bilderdijkgracht, the street continues as the Kwakersstraat, formerly the Kwakersdijk, and the Bellamyplein.

name: Lepelkruisstraat
en: The Lepelkruisstraat is a street in the Weesperbuurt in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Livornostraat
en: The Livornostraat is a street in the Gibraltarbuurt, Landlust district, Amsterdam-West.

name: Loenermark (Amsterdam)
en: Loenermark is a street in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Lutkemeerweg
en: The Lutkemeerweg is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Matterhorn (Amsterdam)
en: The Matterhorn is a street in the De Aker district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies at the end of the Akersingel and is named after the Matterhorn, a mountain in the Walliser Alps. Since 2001 tram line 1 has had its terminus at the Matterhorn in De Aker. In March 2007, during the trial period, the freight tram had its transfer and departure point here.

name: Meibergpad
en: The Meibergpad is a cycle path and street in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It is an important through cycle route in the borough. The path begins at the municipal boundary with Ouder-Amstel, near the cycle bridge over the A2 motorway at the Ouderkerkerplas.

name: Nieuwe Utrechtseweg
en: The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg in Amsterdam is the transition from the S110 to the A2. The road is about 0.5 kilometres long and links the Knooppunt Amstel interchange with the President Kennedylaan. The Utrechtsebrug forms part of the road, which opened with the bridge's entry into use on 1 April 1954. Halfway along the road is an Esso petrol station.

name: Nolensstraat
en: The Nolensstraat is a street in the Van Tijenbuurt and Dudokbuurt of the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. It runs from south to north, from the De Savornin Lohmanstraat to the Sam van Houtenstraat.

name: Noordkaapstraat
en: The Noordkaapstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West about 50 metres long. The street came into being in the early 1980s. As early as 1969, a project group wanted more room for housing in this part of the Spaarndammerbuurt, instead of industry. However, the Wester Suikerraffinaderij sugar refinery stood on the site, in the middle of residential districts.

name: Notweg (Amsterdam)
en: The Notweg is a street in the Amsterdam district of Osdorp. It runs from north to south and begins at the Ookmeerweg. It then crosses the Osdorper Ban and in the south comes to an inglorious end at the Blomwijckerpad and the Groenpad.

name: Olof Palmeplein
en: The Olof Palmeplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord. It lies east of the Buikslotermeerplein, at the junction with the Werengouw and the Th. Weeversweg. The square is part of the Boven 't Y shopping centre and was completed around 1986 as new building and an extension of the shopping centre. Above the shops are homes.

name: Pekkendam
en: Pekkendam is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was named on 3 April 1963 after the Peckedam estate in Diepenheim, which has been a national monument since 12 April 2005. Other streets in the neighbourhood are also named after estates of this kind in the area around Diepenheim.

name: Piri Reisplein
en: The Piri Reisplein is a square in the Amsterdam borough of West, at the Baarsjesweg and the Van Speijkstraat in the Chassébuurt. It is named after the Ottoman Turkish seafarer and cartographer Piri Reïs. In the 20th century the car firm Opel Riva was based here.

name: Plein Spanje '36-'39
en: Plein Spanje '36-'39 is a square in Amsterdam-Noord, in the Volewijck district. The square received its name by council decision of the Noord borough on 8 October 1986. Its name refers to the Spanish Civil War, and the naming was a tribute to the Dutch volunteers who fought in the International Brigades in that war.

name: Plejadenweg
en: The Plejadenweg is a street in Amsterdam-Noord. It is named after the Pleiades star cluster (Zevengesternte). The street is numbered from south-west to north-east, but was built in the reverse order.

name: Ringdijk (Amsterdam)
en: The Ringdijk in Amsterdam-Oost forms the built-up south bank of the north-western part of the Ringvaart of the Watergraafsmeer, between the Middenweg and the Weesperzijde. The opposite bank is called the Transvaalkade. Within the territory of the municipality of Amsterdam, various polders were surrounded by a ring dyke.

name: Robert Fruinlaan
en: The Robert Fruinlaan is an important through street in Slotervaart in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies in line with the Postjesweg and was opened to traffic on 10 July 1960. This required a cutting through the Ringspoorbaan railway. The street runs on to the point where the Johan Huizingalaan becomes the Oostoever.

name: Robert Kochplantsoen
en: The Robert Kochplantsoen is a small park with an associated street in Amsterdam-Oost, in Watergraafsmeer, Tuindorp Frankendael.

name: Rochussenstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Rochussenstraat is a short street in Amsterdam, named after the statesman Jan Jacob Rochussen (1797-1871), successively Minister of Finance, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies and Minister of Colonies. The Rochussenstraat lies in the Staatsliedenbuurt, very close to the GWL site.

name: Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat is a street in the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. It was opened to traffic in 1956 and forms part of the Geuzenveld through ring road. It lies in line with the Antony Moddermanstraat and begins after bridge 627 at the Eendrachtspark, on the border of Slotermeer and Geuzenveld.

name: Scheldeplein
en: The Scheldeplein is an urban square in Amsterdam-Zuid, named after the river Schelde, which flows through France and Flanders and reaches the sea arm of the Westerschelde. The square received its name in 1927. It lies in the Rivierenbuurt, in line with the Scheldestraat, and borders the Europaplein on its south side.

name: Schoolmeesterstraat
en: The Schoolmeesterstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West. By council decision of 7 January 1981 it was named after Gerrit van de Linde, a 19th-century writer who used the pseudonym De Schoolmeester. Several streets in this neighbourhood are named after writers, but nearly a century earlier.

name: Sparrenweg
en: The Sparrenweg is a road in the Oosterparkbuurt in Amsterdam-Oost. The Sparrenweg received its name in 1893, referring to the spruce (spar). The naming was meant to indicate that the Sparrenweg is an important connecting road. The Sparrenweg was, however, a free, narrow street that provided the link between the First and Third Oosterparkstraat.

name: Stoombootweg
en: The Stoombootweg is a street in Amsterdam-Noord. It was originally a footpath beside a ditch in the municipality of Landsmeer. It became more important because from 1867 steamboats began to call at its start, sailing to and from Amsterdam.

name: Sumatraplantsoen
en: The Sumatraplantsoen is a street and small park with square attached in the Indische Buurt in Amsterdam-Oost. It is said to have been the largest square in Amsterdam after the Museumplein.

name: Tweede Sweelinckstraat
en: The Tweede Sweelinckstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The street name is unusual in this district: the others all refer to painters, but the namesake of this street is the composer and organist Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck. The street runs north-south, from the Ceintuurbaan to the Van Ostadestraat.

name: Tweede Van der Helststraat
en: The Tweede Van der Helststraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. It runs from north to south, from the Ceintuurbaan/Sarphatipark to the Joseph Israëlskade on the Amstelkanaal. At the Van der Helstplein the route bends. The street is named after the painter Bartholomeus van der Helst.

name: Van Karnebeekstraat
en: The Van Karnebeekstraat is a street in the Van Tijenbuurt in the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. It runs from the Troelstralaan to the edge of the built-up city, and at the height of the Park de Kuil it becomes the Nico Broekhuysenweg, as far as the Bok de Korverweg, a cycle and footpath.

name: Wamberg (Amsterdam)
en: Wamberg is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was laid out in Cor van Eesteren's General Extension Plan (Algemeen Uitbreidingsplan) for Buitenveldert, and he himself lived there (Weldam 11). Construction of the district began around 1958. Until then the land had been used mainly for arable farming, horticulture and livestock.

name: Weerdestein (Amsterdam)
en: Weerdestein is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Buitenveldert district. It received its name by council decision of 14 June 1961, after Weerdesteyn Castle near Langbroek, Utrecht. The street begins in the north at the Arent Janszoon Ernststraat and ends in the south at a cycle path called the Hinderstein.

name: Werengouw
en: The Werengouw is a street in the Waterlandpleinbuurt (formerly called Nieuwendam-Noord) in Amsterdam-Noord. It received its name by council decisions of 30 October 1963, 2 February 1966 and 3 April 1969. It is named after De Weeren, the grazing area around Zunderdorp.

name: Wijkergouw
en: Wijkergouw is a road in Amsterdam-Noord. A wijk is a linear watercourse, and gouw is an old term for a road alongside a ditch.

name: Willem Mulierhof
en: The Willem Mulierhof is a square in the Van Tijenbuurt in the Geuzenveld district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Willemsstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Willemsstraat is a street and former canal, called the Goudsbloemgracht, in the Amsterdam Jordaan. The street lies between the Brouwersgracht and the Lijnbaansgracht. Between the lifting bridge over the Lijnbaansgracht (bridge no. 142) and the Marnixstraat lies the Nieuwe Willemsstraat. Running parallel to the Willemsstraat is the Goudsbloemstraat.

name: Wolbrantskerkweg
en: The Wolbrantskerkweg is a street in the Amsterdam district of Osdorp. It is a through route for traffic, running east to west, and lies in line with the Koos Vorrinkweg. After the junction with the Tussen Meer the street becomes a residential street, and then curves right and ends in a dead end at the Hoekenes.

name: Daveren
en: Daveren is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It was named on 21 June 1972 after the British city of Dover, which appeared on old Dutch sea charts as Daveren. In Amsterdam Nieuw-West a footpath and cycle path just over 1.5 kilometres long forms the boundary between the Lange Bretten recreation park and the Abberdaan business park.

name: De Cuserstraat
en: De Cuserstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: De Lairessestraat
en: De Lairessestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid was named in 1912 after the 17th-century painter Gerard de Lairesse (1641-1711), who settled in Amsterdam from Liège in 1667. The street runs from the Concertgebouwplein to the Valeriusplein, where it becomes the Cornelis Krusemanstraat.

name: De Leeuw van Vlaanderenstraat
en: De Leeuw van Vlaanderenstraat is a street in Amsterdam West.

name: De Loper
en: De Loper is a street in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: De Rijpstraat
en: De Rijpstraat is a street in the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Landlust. By council decision of 23 March 1922 it was named after the explorer Jan Corneliszoon Rijp (1570-1630), but the street carries the prefix 'De'.

name: Delflandplein
en: The Delflandplein in the Amsterdam borough of Nieuw-West received its name on 30 March 1960. It is named after Delfland, a water board in South Holland bordering Rijnland and Schieland. The square is a pedestrian area lying between the Rijswijkstraat, Overschiestraat, Voorburgstraat and the embankment of the Ringweg-West.

name: Derde Oosterparkstraat
en: The Derde Oosterparkstraat is a shopping and residential street in Amsterdam-Oost. It received its name on 27 February 1895; before that it was known as the Derde Parkstraat. The street is named after the nearby Oosterpark. It is the southernmost of the three Oosterparkstraten and was originally the shortest.

name: Deymanstraat
en: The Deymanstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Dichtershofje
en: Dichtershofje is a relatively short street in Amsterdam Oud-West, in the Bellamybuurt-Zuid neighbourhood.

name: Dijsselhofplantsoen
en: The Dijsselhofplantsoen is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Apollobuurt neighbourhood.

name: Dikninge (Amsterdam)
en: Dikninge is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in Buitenveldert.

name: Diopter
en: Diopter is a street (and also a small neighbourhood) in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Dirk Schäferstraat
en: The Dirk Schäferstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Dirk van Hasseltssteeg
en: The Dirk van Hasseltssteeg is an alley in Amsterdam, running between the Nieuwendijk and the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. It is named after the bargeman Dirk van Hasselt. Archive records show that Van Hasselt himself also owned a corner property in this alley. Foundation remains lie beneath numbers 2 to 6.

name: Dirkshornplantsoen
en: The Dirkshornplantsoen is a small park and also a street in Amsterdam-Noord. The park and street were named on 1 December 1948, after the North Holland village of Dirkshorn. The 200-metre-long park is a sawtooth-shaped strip of greenery between buildings and the ring ditch of the Buikslotermeer.

name: Distelplein
en: The Distelplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Distelweg
en: The Distelweg is a road in the Buiksloterham district of Amsterdam-Noord. It links the Mosplein by Disteldorp and the Van der Pekbuurt with the Distelwegveer ferry, which connects to the Oude Houthaven near the Pontsteiger. The first section of the road was completed in 1918.

name: Donarstraat
en: The Donarstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid. The barely fifty-metre-long street was named by council decision of 19 December 1929, after Thor, known in Dutch as Donar. It begins in the north as a side street of the Argonautenstraat and runs south to the Stadionkade, Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Dora Tamanaplein
en: The Dora Tamanaplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Drie Burgpad
en: The Drie Burgpad is a street and footpath in the De Wetbuurt district of Amsterdam-Oost. It runs through the southern part of De Wetbuurt, which is laid out as green space (gardens and allotments) and sports fields. Those sports fields must of course be reachable by motorised transport.

name: Driehoekstraat
en: The Driehoekstraat is a street in the Amsterdam Jordaan district, lying between the Palmgracht, the Brouwersgracht and the Lijnbaansgracht. It begins at the Palmgracht and runs north. Halfway along, it forks in two: one branch runs left to the Lijnbaansgracht, the other right to the Brouwersgracht.

name: Droogbak (straat)
en: Droogbak is a street and square in Amsterdam-Centrum. The street continues the line of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen in a south-easterly direction, from the Buiten Wieringerstraat to the Singel, where the building of the same name, Droogbak, stands.

name: Duindoornplein
en: The Duindoornplein is a horseshoe-shaped square in Amsterdam-Noord. The Duindoornplein and the Duindoornstraat received their definitive names on 23 July 1930; the street had carried its name since 1922 and was redefined in 1930. Both are named after the sea buckthorn shrub.

name: Durgerdammerdijk
en: The Durgerdammerdijk is a dike and street in the village of Durgerdam in Amsterdam-Noord. The village lies in ribbon development along the dike. The Durgerdammerdijk is part of the Waterlandse Zeedijk, which lay in the former municipality of Ransdorp.

name: Eerste Boerhaavestraat
en: The Eerste Boerhaavestraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Eerste Ceramstraat
en: The Eerste Ceramstraat is a relatively short street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Eerste Coehoornstraat
en: The Eerste Coehoornstraat is a street on the Oostelijke Eilanden in Amsterdam-Centrum. South-east of it lies the Tweede Coehoornstraat, which, contrary to the usual use of ordinal numbers in addresses, neither continues in line with it nor runs parallel. The two streets have no connection with each other.

name: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat
en: The Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat is a street in the Amsterdam borough of West. It lies between the Pesthuysbrug over the Jacob van Lennepkanaal and the Vondelbrug over the Vondelpark.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat
en: Eerste Helmersstraat is a street in the Helmersbuurt in Amsterdam-West.

name: Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat
en: The Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat is a street in the Frederik Hendrikbuurt in Amsterdam-West. By council decision of 30 March 1881 it was named, together with the Tweede and Derde Hugo de Grootstraat, the Hugo de Grootplein and the Hugo de Grootkade/Hugo de Grootgracht. The surrounding district is also known as the Hugo de Grootbuurt.

name: Eerste Jan van der Heijdenstraat
en: The Eerste Jan van der Heijdenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in De Pijp. It runs west to east from the Boerenwetering/Ruysdaelkade to the Ferdinand Bolstraat and then on to the Sarphatipark.

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat is a street in the Jordaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the area between the Laurierstraat and the Lauriergracht and was laid out in the first half of the 17th century as part of the Derde Uitleg (Third Extension) of Amsterdam.

name: Eerste Leeghwaterstraat
en: The Eerste Leeghwaterstraat is a street on the Oostelijke Eilanden in Amsterdam-Centrum, running parallel to the slightly more northerly Tweede Leeghwaterstraat. Named after Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater, it lies between the Conradstraat and the Funenpark and crosses the Czaar Peterstraat, the Blankenstraat and the Kraijenhoffstraat.

name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat
en: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat is a street in the Jordaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the area between the Rozengracht and the Rozenstraat and was laid out in the first half of the 17th century as part of the Derde Uitleg (Third Extension) of Amsterdam.

name: Eerste Sweelinckstraat
en: The Eerste Sweelinckstraat is a street in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid, named after the composer and organist Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck. It runs north to south from the Gerard Doustraat to the Sarphatipark.

name: Eerste van der Helststraat
en: The Eerste van der Helststraat is a street in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It runs north to south from the Stadhouderskade and Singelgracht to the Sarphatipark. The section between the Gerard Doustraat and the Sarphatipark was known around 1900 as the Verlengde van der Helststraat.

name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat
en: The Eerste Van Swindenstraat is a street in the Dapperbuurt of Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Eerste Weteringplantsoen
en: The Eerste Weteringplantsoen is a park and street in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Eikenplein
en: The Eikenplein is a square in Amsterdam-Oost. It received its name in 1912; before that it was an open space on the Eikenweg, which was named in 1882. Both are named after the oak tree, and several streets in the district were named after trees.

name: Emmaplein (Amsterdam)
en: The Emmaplein is an elongated square with a park strip in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Willemsparkbuurt-Noord neighbourhood.

name: Esplanade de Meer
en: Esplanade de Meer is a square in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Etnastraat
en: The Etnastraat is a road in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Fahrenheitstraat
en: The Fahrenheitstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost. Running parallel to it is the Fahrenheitsingel, which forms the boundary between De Wetbuurt and Tuindorp Amstelstation.

name: Falckstraat
en: The Falckstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum, named in 1870 after the statesman, minister and lawyer Anton Reinhard Falck. It lies between the Reguliersgracht and the Frederiksplein. The street's relatively great width results from its being laid out on a section of the Achtergracht that was filled in around 1869.

name: Filips van Almondestraat
en: The Filips van Almondestraat is a relatively short street in the Chassébuurt, Amsterdam-West.

name: Flierbosdreef
en: The Flierbosdreef is a tree-lined avenue (dreef) in the Bijlmermeer district of Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It runs north to south, connecting the Bijlmerdreef near the Bijlmerplein and Anton de Komplein with the Karspeldreef.

name: Floris Versterstraat
en: The Floris Versterstraat is a street in the Hoofddorppleinbuurt neighbourhood, within the Oud-Zuid district of Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Fokke Simonszstraat
en: The Fokke Simonszstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Forintplantsoen
en: The Forintplantsoen is a park in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Frans Halsstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Frans Halsstraat is a street in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Fraunhoferstraat
en: The Fraunhoferstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost, in the Watergraafsmeer district.

name: Fred. Roeskestraat
en: Fred. Roeskestraat is a street on the Zuidas in Amsterdam-Zuid. It received its name on 27 April 1977 and was named after the musician Fred. J. Roeske (1868-1961).

name: Frederik Hendrikstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Frederik Hendrikstraat is a street in the Amsterdam borough of West, between the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen and the Hugo de Grootkade, in line with the Bilderdijkstraat. It is the main traffic artery of the Frederik Hendrikbuurt.

name: Funenkade
en: The Funenkade is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Gaaspstraat
en: The Gaaspstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Rivierenbuurt and Rijnbuurt neighbourhoods.

name: Gaasterlandstraat
en: The Gaasterlandstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Gabriël Metsustraat
en: The Gabriël Metsustraat is a street in the Johannes Vermeerbuurt, in the Museumkwartier of Amsterdam Oud-Zuid.

name: Gedempte Insteekhaven
en: Gedempte Insteekhaven is a street with a small canal in Amsterdam-Noord, in the IJplein neighbourhood.

name: Geelvinckssteeg
en: The Geelvinckssteeg is a small, narrow street in Amsterdam-Centrum. The municipal street sign reads Geelvincksteeg.

name: Geerdinkhof
en: The Geerdinkhof is a sub-district of the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. On 20 January 1971 it was named by council decision after a site in Vasse, in the municipality of Tubbergen in Overijssel.

name: Geertje Wielemaplein
en: The Geertje Wielemaplein is a square in Amsterdam-Oost. It lies on the Zeeburgereiland, the outpost of IJburg north-east of the junction of the Zuiderzeeweg and the IJburglaan, both busy through routes in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Gentiaanplein
en: The Gentiaanplein is a triangular square in Amsterdam-Noord. The square and the associated Gentiaanstraat received their names on 22 March 1922, after the plant genus gentian. It lies in the southern segment at the junction of the Van der Pekstraat and the Johan van Hasseltweg, between the Mosveld and the Hagedoornweg.

name: Gerard Doustraat
en: The Gerard Doustraat is a street in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was named in 1872 after Gerard Dou, the more elegant French form of the name of the 17th-century painter Gerrit Dou.

name: Gerrit van der Veenstraat
en: The Gerrit van der Veenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, about one kilometre long. It runs westward from the Apollolaan to the sports park on the Olympiaplein, crossing the Beethovenstraat, a major traffic artery where tram lines 5 and 24 run, and then the Minervalaan.

name: Gerrit Versteegstraat
en: The Gerrit Versteegstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Noord. It was built on farmland enclosed by De Nieuwe Noorder and the Rijksweg 10 (Ringweg-Noord).

name: Geuzenkade
en: The Geuzenkade is a street in the Amsterdam district of De Baarsjes, not, despite what its name suggests, in Geuzenveld. It is part of the Plan Landlust of 1931 and was built in the 1930s on the former municipal territory of Sloten.

name: Gibraltarstraat
en: The Gibraltarstraat is a street in the Gibraltarbuurt, Landlust, in Amsterdam-West. By council decision of 27 April 1933 it was named after the naval battle off Gibraltar of 25 April 1607.

name: Gillis van Ledenberchstraat
en: The Gillis van Ledenberchstraat is a street in the Frederik Hendrikbuurt in Amsterdam-West. By council decision of 18 July 1919 it was named after Gilles van Ledenberch (1550-1618), clerk to the States of Utrecht and an ally of Johan van Oldenbarnevelt, who had been imprisoned by Prince Maurice.

name: Gouden Leeuw (Amsterdam)
en: Gouden Leeuw is a street and apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The street, building and surrounding area were designated a municipal monument in 2021 (number 200956). The complex has a similar building in Groenhoven.

name: Goudriaanstraat
en: The Goudriaanstraat is a street in the Van der Kunbuurt of Amsterdam-Oost. It received its name by council decision on 26 July 1939, after the engineer Bernardus Hermanus Goudriaan of Rijkswaterstaat, a colleague of Leopold Johannes Adriaan van der Kun, after whom the neighbourhood and the Van der Kunstraat are named.

name: Graafschapstraat
en: The Graafschapstraat is a relatively short street in the Landstrekenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. By council decision on 26 July 1939 it was named after the alternative name of the Achterhoek region, De Graafschap. It was redefined in 1951 and 1964.

name: Gravenstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Gravenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum, linking the Nieuwendijk with the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. Halfway along, it is crossed to the south by the Eggertstraat (until 1865 the Ellendigesteeg) and to the north by the Blaeustraat.

name: Groenhoven (Amsterdam)
en: Groenhoven is a street and apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The street, building and surrounding area were designated a municipal monument in 2021 (number 200956). It has a sibling building in Gouden Leeuw.

name: Gulden Winckelplantsoen
en: The Gulden Winckelplantsoen is an open space in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Gustav Mahlerlaan
en: The Gustav Mahlerlaan is a street in the residential and business district of the Zuidas in Amsterdam-Zuid. It runs from the De Boelelaan to the Beethovenstraat and crosses the Buitenveldertselaan. In 1998 it was named after the Austrian composer and conductor Gustav Mahler.

name: Gustav Mahlerplein
en: The Gustav Mahlerplein is a square with a pedestrian area in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was named after the composer and conductor Gustav Mahler on 17 December 2002. All the streets and squares in the district are named after composers.

name: H. Stolleplantsoen
en: H. Stolleplantsoen is a city park with an associated street in Amsterdam-Noord. The park section is about 370 metres long and just over 30 metres wide.

name: Haarlemmer Houttuinen
en: The Haarlemmer Houttuinen was a former neighbourhood, and since 1973 has been the name of a street in the Haarlemmerbuurt in Amsterdam-Centrum. The street was laid out around 1970 after the old buildings were demolished, linking the Haarlemmerplein with the Droogbak.

name: Hagedoornplein
en: Hagedoornplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Halvemaansteeg
en: The Halvemaansteeg is a short alley in the centre of Amsterdam, linking the Rembrandtplein with the Amstel at the Halvemaansbrug. Like the name of that bridge, the alley's name probably derives from the building at number 18, which bears the inscription 'Van Ouds de Halve Maan'.

name: Handboogstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Handboogstraat is a narrow street in Amsterdam-Centrum, between the Spui and the Heiligeweg. It lies behind Singel 421-425, the University Library of Amsterdam, and runs parallel to the Voetboogstraat and the Kalverstraat. It is mistakenly also called the Handboogsteeg.

name: Hannie Dankbaarpassage
en: The Hannie Dankbaarpassage is a short passage in the Bellamybuurt in Amsterdam-West.

name: Harmoniehof
en: The Harmoniehof is a street in Amsterdam Oud-Zuid. It forms part of a large complex of middle-class housing lying between the Roelof Hartstraat, Hobbemakade, Reijnier Vinkeleskade and Joh. M. Coenenstraat. Architect J.C. van Epen was commissioned to design the complex, in collaboration with architect M.J.E. Lippits.

name: Hartelstein
en: Hartelstein is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid. This back street received its name on 13 May 1959, after Kasteel Hartelstein. Several streets in the Buitenveldert neighbourhood are named after castles and country houses. Other towns, including Maastricht and Eindhoven, also have a Hartelstein street.

name: Hartenstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Hartenstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum. It probably dates from the mid-17th century and in the 21st century forms part of the De 9 Straatjes district. In the past it was an exit road from the centre of Amsterdam towards the western part of the city centre.

name: Hazenstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Hazenstraat is a relatively short street (150 metres) in the Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum. It is also called the '10th little street', as a supplement to the Negen Straatjes (Nine Streets).

name: Heemstedestraat
en: The Heemstedestraat is a street that lies in both Amsterdam-Zuid and Nieuw-West.

name: Heesterveld
en: Heesterveld is a street in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Heining
en: Heining, colloquially known as De Heining, is a complex of streets in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Hekelveld
en: The Hekelveld is a relatively small square in Amsterdam-Centrum, at the northern end of the Spuistraat. On its eastern side the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal becomes the Martelaarsgracht. The building at Hekelveld 1 dates from the 18th century and is designated a national monument.

name: Hemonylaan
en: The Hemonylaan is an avenue in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was named in 1891 after Pieter and François Hemony, bell-founders. It was built over the Zaagmolensloot, which was filled in at the end of the 19th century, and the former waterway is still visible in the street's unusual width for the district.

name: Hemonystraat
en: The Hemonystraat is a street in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was named in 1880 after Pieter and François Hemony, bell-founders. It runs at right angles to the Hemonylaan, which was named ten years later.

name: Hempontplein
en: The Hempontplein is the unofficial name of a ferry square in the Western Harbour Area of Amsterdam. Colloquially it is named after the Hempont, the ferry that sails here between Amsterdam and Zaandam. That ferry is indirectly named after the former headland of the Hem in the old IJ, south of Zaandam.

name: Hemsterhuisstraat
en: The Hemsterhuisstraat is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Henrick de Keijserplein
en: The Henrick de Keijserplein is a square in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Henrick de Keijserstraat
en: The Henrick de Keijserstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Henriëtte Ronnerplein
en: The Henriëtte Ronnerplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Herderhof
en: Herderhof is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is both a courtyard (hofje) and a street.

name: Herenmarkt
en: The Herenmarkt is a square and street in Amsterdam-Centrum, forming a rectangular recess between the Brouwersgracht and the Haarlemmerstraat. There is a playground on the Herenmarkt. The West-Indisch Huis stands on the square; it was built in 1617 as a meat hall and waiting room for the civic guard.

name: Het Dok
en: Het Dok is a street in the form of a square in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Hildo Kropplein
en: The Hildo Kropplein is a square in the Oostelijk Havengebied (Eastern Docklands) of Amsterdam-Oost. It arose when the Cruquiuseiland was redeveloped from harbour land into a residential district, and much of the commercial premises gave way to homes and shops.

name: Hobbemastraat
en: The Hobbemastraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid between the Stadhouderskade and the Hobbemakade. It received its name in 1880 and was named after Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), a Dutch landscape painter.

name: Hoekenrode
en: Hoekenrode, colloquially also called Hoekenrodeplein, is a large square between the Amsterdamse Poort and Bijlmer ArenA station, in the Bijlmermeer district of Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The Nieuw Amsterdam building on Hoekenrode houses a Hampton by Hilton hotel, Vattenfall and several bars and restaurants.

name: Hoekschewaardplein
en: The Hoekschewaardplein is a square in Amsterdam-Noord. The square and the Hoekschewaardweg lie in Tuindorp Buiksloot, in the small district of Blauwe Zand, a name that refers to the blue colour of the sand that was pumped in at the time. The name lives on in the Blauwezandbrug.

name: Hogevecht
en: Hogevecht is a street in the Bijlmermeer district of Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Along it stand the blocks of flats Hogevecht Oost and Hogevecht West, squeezed between the Abcouderpad and the Flierbosdreef.

name: Hogeweg (Amsterdam)
en: The Hogeweg is a street in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Holendrechtplein
en: The Holendrechtplein is the central square of the Holendrecht district in the Amsterdam district of Zuidoost.

name: Holendrechtstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Holendrechtstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid (Oud-Zuid), in the IJselbuurt-Oost neighbourhood.

name: Hollandse Tuin (Amsterdam)
en: Hollandse Tuin is a street in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Hondecoeterstraat
en: The Hondecoeterstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Museumkwartier. A neighbourhood, the Hondecoeterbuurt, was named after the street.

name: Hondsrugweg (Amsterdam)
en: The Hondsrugweg is a wide road in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The 750-metre road is known in Amsterdam as the road between the Johan Cruijff Arena and IKEA.

name: Honselersdijkstraat
en: The Honselersdijkstraat is a street in the Westlandgracht district of Slotervaart, in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Honthorststraat
en: The Honthorststraat is a street in the Museumkwartier, Amsterdam-Zuid. By council decision of 10 June 1880 it was named after the painter Gerard van Honthorst. Several street names in the Museumkwartier honour painters, and several other cities also have streets named after him.

name: Hoofddorpplein
en: The Hoofddorpplein lies in the Hoofddorppleinbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is connected via the Hoofddorpweg and the Zeilbrug to the area around the Amstelveenseweg. The square was named in 1927 after Hoofddorp in the Haarlemmermeer, and the streets in the neighbourhood are named after places south-west of Amsterdam.

name: Hoofdweg (Amsterdam)
en: The Hoofdweg is a street in Amsterdam-West, lined with residential buildings mostly designed in the style of the Amsterdam School. It runs from the Surinameplein to the Bos en Lommerplein, through the Baarsjes and Bos en Lommer districts, and crosses the Postjesweg, the Jan Evertsenstraat and the Jan van Galenstraat.

name: Hoogoorddreef
en: The Hoogoorddreef is a through road in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Its first section is a tree-lined avenue on raised ground, opened to through traffic in 1971 as an access road for the first Bijlmer station. It runs from the Flierbosdreef west past the Amsterdamse Poort shopping centre and crosses the Foppingadreef.

name: Hoogte Kadijk
en: The Hoogte Kadijk is a street and embankment on the Kadijkseiland in Amsterdam. It links the Kadijksplein with the Sarphatistraat. Parallel to it run the Laagte Kadijk to the south and the Nieuwe Vaart to the north. Side streets are the Buiten Kadijken and the Tussen Kadijken.

name: Hudsonhof
en: The Hudsonhof is a small pedestrian area in De Baarsjes, Amsterdam-West.

name: Hugo de Grootplein (Amsterdam)
en: The Hugo de Grootplein is a square and traffic roundabout in Amsterdam-West. It forms the centre of the Hugo de Grootbuurt, which is part of the Frederik Hendrikbuurt. The square and surrounding streets were named in 1881 after Hugo de Groot (1584-1645).

name: Iepenplein
en: The Iepenplein is a square in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: IJplein (plein)
en: The IJplein is a square in the IJplein neighbourhood, officially IJplein and surroundings, in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Immanuel Kanthof
en: Immanuel Kanthof is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Imogirituin
en: The Imogirituin is a square in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Ingenhouszhof
en: The Ingenhouszhof is a street in Amsterdam-Oost, in the Tuindorp Frankendael neighbourhood of Watergraafsmeer.

name: Ir. Jakoba Mulderplein
en: The Ir. Jakoba Mulderplein is a square in Amsterdam-Centrum. Named in 1990, it lies wedged between the Sarphatistraat and the Singelgracht, with its Alexanderkade. It came about after a large-scale renovation of the buildings in and around the Zeeburgerstraat.

name: Isaac Titsinghkade
en: The Isaac Titsinghkade is a quay in Amsterdam-Centrum, accessible to pedestrians and cyclists only. It is named after Isaac Titsingh, a senior official of the Dutch East India Company (VOC), which once had its warehouses here. The quay forms the bank of the Oostenburgervaart for only part of its length.

name: Iseoplantsoen
en: The Iseoplantsoen is a park in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: J.F. Berghoefplantsoen
en: The J.F. Berghoefplantsoen is a small park and associated streets in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. On 2 December 1997 it was named by council decision after the architect Johannes Fake Berghoef.

name: J.J. Cremerplein
en: The J.J. Cremerplein is a square in Amsterdam-West.

name: Jaagpad (Amsterdam)
en: The Amsterdam Jaagpad is a remnant of the old passenger barge (trekschuit) route between Amsterdam and Leiden. The towpath runs along part of the Schinkel, from the Sloterkade/Rijnsburgstraat, and the Nieuwe Meer. Before 1921 this area belonged to the municipality of Sloten.

name: Jacob Bontiusplaats
en: Jacob Bontiusplaats is a topographical designation in Amsterdam-Centrum on Oostenburg. It lies between the Wittenburgervaart with its VOC-kade and the Oostenburgervaart with its Isaac Titsinghkade. The site once served as the factory grounds of Werkspoor and Stork and was decontaminated and redeveloped around 2000.

name: Jacob Catskade
en: The Jacob Catskade in Amsterdam-West consists of built-up quays on either side of the waterway known as the 'Kattensloot'. It runs south-west from the Kattenslootbrug at the Nassaukade to the Van der Palmkade in the Staatsliedenbuurt.

name: Jacob Geelstraat
en: The Jacob Geelstraat is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It runs north to south from the Hemsterhuisstraat to the Comeniusstraat.

name: Jacob Marisplein
en: The Jacob Marisplein is a square in the Hoofddorppleinbuurt, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Jacoba Mosselhof
